actual.ambiguous_interval_scope: 33 S3 requests have multiple compatible original HTTP intervals. The auditor checks legal interval/version constraints; it does not claim unique per-request HTTP attribution.
actual.environment_observation: The SeaweedFS version command emitted netlink permission warnings. Backend readiness, signed object operations and all fixed oracles subsequently passed; this was not counted as a product fault injection.
observed_contracts: Two same-database Query calls enter distinct original HEAD GET holds before either release.
Another tenant Query, the database writer and a control status each finish while both reads remain held.
A queued same-tenant Query waits for active capacity to be released.
Two other-tenant reader holds leave exactly one worker for warm and refresh; stale refresh performs exactly three HEAD GETs and observes row 3.
A single pre-forward HEAD blackhole yields UNKNOWN without another POST, another S3 request or object write in that phase.
An INSERT through Query returns ENGINE, publishes no objects and leaves row 99 absent.
Revoking the reader permission makes the next authenticated Query return DENIED.
Three original-identity lookups return byte-identical original random results and receipts.
Original HTTP and S3 ledgers match final relay high-water counters.
Private database files have distinct device/inode pairs and worker directories.
Service and SDK exit normally; all cache files are cleaned; four owned backend children are reaped with kernel wait4 witnesses.

boundaries.retained_cache_budget: workers * pages_per_actor bounds retained cache after an operation, not peak physical disk or memory.
boundaries.sql_replay: Only a pre-SQL StaleSnapshot may rebuild once under the original deadline; no arbitrary query or write replay.
boundaries.writer_model: One serial writer actor per HEAD; independent complete private images for the read pool.

build.receipt_hash_difference: The archived receipt adds archive witness bindings; it retains the original Cargo evidence, source inputs and release binary identity.
